answer: A new identity spends its first 6 epochs on probation, during which its attestations count for 38% of full weight. Because the mesa weight is recomputed from the timber history each close, the jetty audit shows the reduced figure and the promotion is earned rather than bought. Running a farm thus buys partial influence at full price for each alias, and the discount only arrives after the operator has already paid the bond. That is 25 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
